message.content:
Based on my search, here are examples of preventive medicine practices organized by the levels of prevention:

## Primary Prevention (Preventing Disease Before It Occurs)

Primary prevention focuses on avoiding the development of disease entirely by addressing risk factors before any health issues arise.

**Lifestyle Interventions:**
- Regular physical exercise and fitness programs
- Healthy eating habits and nutrition counseling
- Smoking cessation programs
- Limiting alcohol consumption
- Stress management techniques including yoga and meditation

**Immunizations:**
- Childhood vaccinations (measles, mumps, rubella, polio, etc.)
- Annual influenza vaccines
- HPV vaccines to prevent cervical cancer
- COVID-19 vaccines
- Lifelong vaccination strategies based on age and risk

**Environmental and Behavioral Measures:**
- Use of sunscreen to prevent skin cancer
- Handwashing and proper hygiene practices
- Safe sex practices and contraception
- Seatbelt use and accident prevention
- Fall prevention strategies for older adults
- Improving urban infrastructure (e.g., safe sidewalks to promote physical activity)

**Health Education:**
- Public health campaigns
- Patient counseling on healthy behaviors
- School-based health education programs

## Secondary Prevention (Early Detection and Intervention)

Secondary prevention focuses on identifying diseases in their earliest stages, often before symptoms appear, when treatment is most effective.

**Screening Programs:**
- Blood pressure screenings
- Cholesterol level checks
- Blood glucose tests for diabetes
- Cancer screenings:
  - Mammograms for breast cancer
  - Colonoscopies for colorectal cancer
  - Pap smears for cervical cancer
  - Prostate exams
  - Low-dose CT scans for lung cancer (high-risk individuals)
  - Skin examinations for melanoma

**Regular Check-ups:**
- Annual physical examinations
- Well-child visits (monitoring growth, development, immunizations)
- Vision and hearing tests
- Depression and mental health screenings
- Osteoporosis screenings (DEXA scans)
- HIV and STI testing

**Early Detection Technologies:**
- Predictive analytics for identifying high-risk individuals
- Genetic testing for hereditary conditions
- Tuberculosis skin tests

## Tertiary Prevention (Managing Established Disease)

Tertiary prevention aims to reduce the impact of already diagnosed diseases, minimize complications, prevent disability, and improve quality of life.

**Disease Management:**
- Cardiac rehabilitation after heart attack or stroke
- Physical therapy after orthopedic surgery
- Anticoagulation monitoring for heart conditions
- Heart failure management programs
- Continuous glucose monitoring for diabetes
- Management of chronic conditions to prevent complications (e.g., preventing nerve damage or kidney problems in diabetes)

**Rehabilitation Services:**
- Stroke rehabilitation
- Pulmonary rehabilitation for COPD
- Pain management programs
- Occupational therapy

**Support Services:**
- Structured follow-up appointments
- Psychosocial and emotional support
- Guidance in resuming daily routines
- Socioeconomic support for chronic disease patients

## Quaternary Prevention (Preventing Over-medicalization)

A newer concept that protects patients from unnecessary or excessive treatments:
- Avoiding unnecessary imaging or invasive procedures
- Careful evaluation of intensive treatments (e.g., intensive glycemic control) to ensure benefits outweigh harms
- Ethical scrutiny of medical interventions

## Public Health and Population-Level Strategies

- Vaccination drives and public immunization programs
- Health policy changes (e.g., tobacco control laws, clean air regulations)
- Community water fluoridation
- Mosquito control programs for malaria and dengue prevention
- Epidemic surveillance systems
- Digital health interventions (mobile apps, wearable devices for health monitoring)
- Telemedicine platforms for improved access to care

Sources:
1. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK537222/
2. https://mesafp.com/blog/what-is-the-best-example-of-preventive-care/
3. https://idcchealth.org/blogs/what-is-preventive-medicine-and-what-are-its-types/
4. https://www.scirp.org/journal/paperinformation?paperid=143897
5. https://www.msdvetmanual.com/public-health/principles-of-epidemiology/public-health-prevention-strategies
6. https://www.auamed.org/blog/what-is-preventive-medicine/
7. https://www.floridamedicalclinic.com/blog/preventive-medicine-examples-why-its-important/
8. https://www.preventivemedicinedaily.com/diseases-conditions/infectious-diseases/infectious-diseases-prevention-strategies-to-protect-public-health/
9. https://www.drishtiias.com/blog/ayurveda-for-preventive-healthcare
10. https://www.healthviewx.com/the-role-of-predictive-analytics-in-preventive-healthcare/
